title: Hobbycast Episode 5: Video Podcast - Asian Cinema Nostalgia - Part 1
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dtdf5AeXwB8

The first video podcast on the channel, and the start of a long one. Daniel (@dungeondive) hauls out the binders holding his Asian cinema DVD collection, mostly Hong Kong martial arts, and starts flipping through the sleeves in whatever order they came out of the box. He opens with two confessions: for the old Black Belt Theater-era films he genuinely prefers the dubs, purely for nostalgia, and he stopped intensely following the genre around 2010, so the encyclopaedic recall is gone.

What follows is roughly 48 covers with a story attached to each. *Hero* in its uncut director's version. *Terracotta Warrior*, a holy grail that turned out boring. *Once Upon a Time in China*, rented on two VHS tapes from an Asian video store in Fresno, the film that pulled him from Black Belt Theater into 90s wire-fu. *Butterfly and Sword*, where a swordsman fires himself from his own bow into a cavalry charge and a carload of skater kids resolved to track down every wire-fu movie in town. Along the way: Tsui Hark as the Spielberg-on-*Poltergeist* producer, the Suncoast Video Sunday ritual of always buying two discs in case the first one was bad, Wong Jing's swordsmen with wings, *Mr. Vampire*, *Boxer's Omen*, and *Project A* as the best Jackie Chan film ever made.

----

Daniel prefers the old dubs on classic kung fu films for nostalgia alone. Is there a genre where you'd defend the "wrong" version too?
